slot.brief: Which statement about ozone depletion is incorrect (e.g. role of CFCs, Cl radical chain, NO catalysis)?

stem: Which statement about stratospheric ozone depletion is incorrect?
options: CFCs can reach the stratosphere because they are relatively unreactive in the lower atmosphere.
Ultraviolet radiation can photolyse CFCs and release chlorine radicals.
Nitrogen oxide radicals can participate in catalytic cycles that destroy ozone.
A chlorine radical is consumed in each ozone-destruction step and cannot be regenerated.

verdicts.working: Chlorine radicals react with ozone but are regenerated in catalytic cycles, so they are not consumed permanently.

working:
$\text{Cl}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{ClO}+\text{O}_2$
$\text{ClO}+\text{O}\rightarrow\text{Cl}+\text{O}_2$
Net: $\text{O}_3+\text{O}\rightarrow2\text{O}_2$
The chlorine radical is regenerated, so it acts catalytically.

Independent check: Chlorine radicals react with ozone but are regenerated in catalytic cycles, so they are not consumed permanently.
solution:
Chlorine radicals destroy ozone through a catalytic cycle:
$$\text{Cl}+\text{O}_3\rightarrow\text{ClO}+\text{O}_2,\qquad \text{ClO}+\text{O}\rightarrow\text{Cl}+\text{O}_2$$
Since $\text{Cl}$ is regenerated, it is not consumed permanently; hence statement (D) is incorrect.
